description: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine-shaped warmdown schedule.
Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 to prevent the learning rate from dropping to zero during the warmdown phase.
Increase the warmdown ratio from 0.5 to 0.7 to extend the learning rate decay period.
Reduce DEPTH from 8 to 6 (model_dim stays 384 at ASPECT_RATIO 64) so each step is cheaper and the model gets more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.

issues: The diff changes one hyperparameter: DEPTH goes from 8 to 6. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the prepare.py import line, the seed lines or the evaluation call and summary printing. No integrity flags were raised.

I couldn't recompute z exactly because the incumbent's per-run standard deviation, or the z formula, isn't given. The means are consistent with the claim: the candidate mean is 1.08305 and the incumbent mean is 1.1145, so the candidate is lower by 0.03145. A z of 7.655 implies a standard error of about 0.0041, which is plausible. The decision to accept matches the direction of the numbers.

Note: if the model width is derived from DEPTH (aspect ratio), the candidate is a smaller model. A smaller model gets more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, which plausibly explains the gain. That is a legitimate change, not a bug. The two candidate runs agree closely (1.0828 and 1.0833).

description: Reduce DEPTH from 8 to 6 (model_dim stays 384 at ASPECT_RATIO 64) so each step is cheaper and the model gets more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Increase DEPTH from 6 to 10 (model_dim becomes 640 with 5 heads at ASPECT_RATIO 64) to test whether the larger model beats the faster-stepping shallower one within the fixed time budget.

issues: (1) Measurement integrity: the diff changes only one line. It adds mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' to torch.compile. It does not touch val_bpb, the data, the tokenizer, the prepare.py import line, the two seed lines, the evaluation call or the final summary printing. I found no attempt to change how the score is measured.
(2) Bugs: none that would make a result meaningless. Autotuning only picks different matmul kernels. These can change floating-point results slightly but do not change the model's maths.

The harness rejected the run for integrity flags but gave no detail. The most likely cause is the 450 s limit on startup plus training. max-autotune benchmarks many kernel candidates during compile, which can add minutes. The other possibility is that the harness counts any change to how the evaluated model is compiled as an altered evaluation path, since evaluation probably runs through the compiled model.
(3) Claims: the run produced no val_bpb or variance figures, so z cannot be recomputed and no improvement can be confirmed. The result cannot be accepted as it stands.

Recommendation: drop this change, or limit the cost of autotuning so startup plus training stays well under 450 s. Expected gains in a 300 s run are small either way. The extra compile option is weak on the simplicity criterion and should not be retried without a reason to expect a gain.

description: Compile the model with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' so that faster kernels can yield more optimizer steps within the 300 s training budget.

issues: None found. The diff changes one hyperparameter: HEAD_DIM goes from 128 to 64, which doubles the number of attention heads at the same model_dim. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines or the evaluation call, and the integrity flags are empty.
No bugs found that would make the result meaningless. HEAD_DIM=64 divides model_dim = depth*64 for any depth, so the head count stays a whole number.

I could not recompute z exactly. The two individual incumbent runs and their spread are not given. The direction is consistent: the candidate (1.0894) is 0.0063 worse than the incumbent mean (1.0831), so z is negative. The reported z = -0.937 implies a standard error of about 0.0067, which is plausible but can't be checked here. The reject decision matches the numbers.
Only one candidate run was made, so this weak result is not conclusive. It still gives no reason to spend a replicate slot.

description: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so the depth-6, 384-dim model gets 6 attention heads of size 64 instead of 3 heads of size 128.
Shorten the Muon momentum ramp from 300 steps to 100 steps and raise the final maximum momentum to 0.97.
Reduce the MLP hidden expansion from 4x to 3x n_embd so each step is cheaper and the 300 s budget buys more steps.
Increase Muon matrix learning rate from 0.04 to 0.06 and reduce Newton-Schulz polynomial degree from 5 to 4 to balance step speed and fit.
Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSS" so all layers except the forced-full final layer use half-context sliding windows, to measure the speed gain from cheaper attention.

Keep an EMA (decay 0.999, updated each step via torch._foreach_lerp_) of all model parameters and copy it into the model just before the final evaluation call; the eval call and summary printing are untouched.
Set DEPTH from 6 to 4 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 128 so model_dim is 512 with 4 heads of size 128, leaving everything else unchanged.
Implement a small LR warmup (5%), a larger warmdown (40%), and a non-zero final LR fraction (0.05) to stabilize and sustain training performance.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff changes one hyperparameter: WARMDOWN_RATIO goes from 0.5 to 0.3. It doesn't touch the evaluation call, the data, the prepare.py import line or the seed lines. It doesn't add a bug that would make the result meaningless.

I can't check the z value independently. The harness gives the incumbent mean (1.0831, n=2) but not the two individual runs or their spread, and there is only one candidate run, so there is nothing to estimate variance from. The reported z = -0.073 does have the right sign: the candidate (1.0836) is 0.0005 worse, since lower is better. It would also mean a spread of about 0.007, which is plausible.
The decision is consistent with the numbers. The candidate is slightly worse and well within noise, so rejecting it is reasonable.

description: Decrease the warmdown ratio from 0.5 to 0.3 to keep the learning rate at its peak for a longer portion of the training time.
Lower the logit softcap constant in the forward pass from 15 to 10, keeping the tanh form unchanged, to test whether a tighter logit cap stabilizes training in a short run.
Set MATRIX_LR to 0.05 and introduce a 3% LR warmup to stabilize the higher learning rate.
Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 to increase parameter update strength for matrix parameters.

The attention and MLP output projections (c_proj) are already zero-initialized, so per the spec's fallback I lower the resid_lambdas init from 1.0 to 0.9; the spec calls these the x0 skip scalars, but the 0.1-initialized x0_lambdas are a separate parameter, so I left them unchanged.
